rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover the ground truth's core concern (the CUDA-only gate was widened from `==cuda` to `!=cpu`, sweeping in unvalidated accelerators like NPU/XPU) and both catch a real, diff-grounded FL2VA/Ref2VA doc mismatch. X goes further with a technically verified, high-value catch Y misses entirely (fork_rng's `device_type` kwarg defaults to "cuda" and doesn't derive from the `devices` list, so the fix silently mis-saves/restores RNG state), and presents every finding with precise line numbers and ready-to-apply diffs. Y's output is comparably grounded but structurally weaker: several "major" findings literally show `vae.py:?` as the file:line header (failing the concrete-location bar) and some points are left as open questions rather than actionable fixes. Neither includes a labeled LATENT GAP CHECK section.
